goal: prove c(n) = (n+2)/3 only for n = 1 and primes p = 1 (mod 6) (c = number of cubes mod n)
obstacle: Counting bounds settle every n except two Diophantine cases: (A) n = pB with p = 1 (mod 6) prime and B > 1 built from primes = 2 (mod 3), equation p(B - c(B)) = 2(c(B) - 1), no solution for B <= 10^12; (B) all prime factors = 2 (mod 3), equation 3c(n) = n + 2. In case B, c(n)/n lies on both sides of 1/3 (e.g. n = 2^4 * prod q^2 over q = 2 mod 3, q <= 317, is below), so no one-sided bound works. No congruence obstruction mod M <= 72. The triage note assumed c(q^e) = q^e for q = 2 (mod 3), true only for e = 1 (c(25) = 21).
next: Exact arithmetic on the two equations (case B counterexamples would exceed about 10^30); likely hard. Triage score lowered.

goal: Lean proof that |a(n)|^(1/n) -> infinity (mean of log prime gaps -> infinity)

Chebyshev bounds alone cannot work: a set with pi(x) ~ x/log x can have almost all gaps equal to 2. A fixed-level sieve gives densities 1/log^2 y, too weak.
next: Formalise a Selberg/Brun upper bound for prime pairs (would also close OEIS-A215462 conjecture 2).

goal: prove #{0<a<=b<=c : a^2+b^2+c^2 = 9^n} = (3^n+2n-1)/4 in Lean (corrected indexing)
obstacle: Everything reduces in Lean (descent by 3, A047926_iff) to the primitive count P(n) = (3^(n-1)+1)/2, i.e. Gauss-Hurwitz r_3(9^n) = 6(2*3^n-1). Mathlib has no r_3 formula. Elementary alternative considered: the 4-regular Hecke tree of primitive points (parent map via integer matrices M with M M^T = 9I, e.g. [[1,2,2],[2,1,-2],[2,-2,1]]); needs uniqueness of the parent and exactly 3 children per vertex, a mod-9/27 case analysis not attempted. The binary part (2a^2+c^2 = 9^n has n positive solutions) is elementary (uniqueness of the primitive solution via 9^n | (y1x2-x1y2)(y1x2+x1y2)) but unneeded.

goal: prove that k with A046530(k) = (k+2)/3 (offset 1, a(1) = 1) are exactly 1 and the primes p = 1 (mod 6); c = number of cubes mod k
obstacle: The local bounds give the easy part: c is multiplicative, c(p) = (p+2)/3 for p = 1 (mod 6), c(p^e)/p^e < 1/3 for p = 1 (mod 3) and e >= 2, two such primes give (p+2)(p'+2)/(9pp') < 1/3, and 3 does not divide k. That leaves the same two cases as the first attempt. Case B (every prime factor q = 2 mod 3, 3c(n) = n+2) and case A (n = pB, B such a product, (p+2)c(B) = pB+2). The method needs a one-sided local factor. For the squares siblings the 3-adic factor supplied it (3 | n). Here no prime divides n with a fixed local ratio. Each factor c(q^e)/q^e lies between 1 - 1/q and 1 - 1/q + 1/q^2, and products of these cross 1/3 (case B) and cross p/(p+2) (case A). So the method fails at the first step after the reduction. Alternative route tried: congruences. They exclude 2 || n (n+2 = 0 mod 4 but 3c(n) = 2 mod 4), 2^e || n with e >= 2 unless e = 1 (mod 3) (c(2^e) is odd otherwise), and odd q^e || n with e = 1 (mod 3) (then q | c(n), so q | n+2). They also give c(q^2) = q^2-q+1 = 3 * unit mod 9, so n+2 needs one factor of 3 per squared prime, and c(q^e) | n+2 for each q^e || n. None of these is a contradiction. The remaining equations look like Lehmer's totient problem (phi(n) | n-1): a product of local factors must hit a rational target exactly.
evidence: work/tier2/A123365/probe.py: c(q^e) = 1 + sum over j = e, e-3, ... >= 1 of phi(q^j) (q = 2 mod 3) and c(p^e) = 1 + sum phi(p^j)/3 (p = 1 mod 3) match brute force. Brute force to k < 4000 finds only 1 and primes 1 mod 6. Case A with B = q^a r^b (5 <= q < r < 3000, q, r = 2 mod 3, a, b in {2,3,5,6}) has no prime p = 1 (mod 6). Single prime power B = q^e: p = 2(c-1)/(q^e - c), not an integer prime 1 mod 6 for e = 2 (p = 2q), 3 (p = 2q^2/(q+1)) or 5 (p = 2q(q^3+1)/(q^3+q^2+1)). OEIS entry unchanged (2022 revision, still a conjecture). formal-conjectures has no OEIS/123365.lean (tree listing 2026-11-05). A web search found no proof.
next: Treat it as a Lehmer-type problem. Bound the number of prime factors of B in case A (each factor q > about p/2, and the defect sum must equal 2(B-1)/((p+2)B)), and look for a sieve as in the Lehmer totient literature. A full proof is unlikely with local bounds alone. Lean for the reduction (every prime 1 mod 6 is a term, and other terms fall in cases A or B) could be done by adapting A123722_mathlib.lean, but it would not settle the conjecture.

goal: no composite n with phi(n) | n - 1; failing that, the strongest weaker result in Lean
obstacle: Proved in Lean: a Lehmer number is squarefree, odd, Carmichael, has at least 4 distinct prime factors, and with K prime factors n <= (2K)^(2^K - 1), so finitely many for each K. The gap argument (n - 1 = m phi(n), m >= 2, so m phi(A) >= A + 1 for every proper prefix A of the ordered primes) bounds each prime by k(A + 1) in terms of the smaller primes only; nothing bounds K. This is the known barrier (literature: omega >= 14-15, count O(x^{1/2}(log x)^{3/4})). Extending omega >= 4 to 5 by kernel decide needs about 18000 prime triples with the last prime fixed by the exact equation; not attempted (time box; omega >= 7 is classical).
evidence: work/famous/lehmer/Lehmer_mathlib.lean (prime_lt_of_isLehmer, le_bound_of_isLehmer, finite_isLehmer_card, four_le_card_of_isLehmer); axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; scripts/lehmer_checks.py (no composite n < 10^6)

method_name: Local bounds for multiplicative counts + mod-q valuation of c(q^e)
goal: classify n with at most 2 distinct prime factors and 3c(n) = n + 2 (c = number of cubes mod n); show (p+2)c(q^e) = p q^e + 2 has no solution with p prime = 1 mod 6, q = 2 mod 3
obstacle: Done: omega(n) <= 2 classified (solutions only 1 and primes 1 mod 6) and the prime-power equation has no solution (for any prime p the only one is p = 3, B = 16). Key step: the equation is (p+2) s1 = p G with G = 1 (mod q) and s1 = 0, 1, q (mod q) by e mod 3; this forces q = p (impossible) or q = 2, e = 3t+1, then (8^t - 1)(3p - 8) = 7. In Lean the Diophantine part is unconditional; the two-factor theorem is conditional on the closed forms of c at prime powers and multiplicativity, which are not formalised (would need the structure of (Z/q^e)^* and the non-unit cubes; not attempted in the time box).
evidence: work/famous/lehmer/CubesTwoFactors_mathlib.lean (cq_equation_no_solution, three_c_eq_one_factor, three_c_ne_of_two_factors); scripts/cube_checks.py (closed forms vs brute force; prime-power search q < 2000, e <= 12; n < 20000)

method_name: Lehmer-type gap argument for fixed K
goal: for fixed K >= 3, finitely many n with K distinct prime factors and 3c(n) = n + 2 (core-multiplicative-exact-target)
obstacle: The Lehmer gap (3c(A) >= A + 1 for a proper part A, else 3c(n) <= A c(B) < n + 2) bounds the smallest prime of the cofactor in terms of A, but (i) in case A (n = pB) the prime p = 1 mod 3 has local ratio about 1/3, so it sets the target p/(p+2) for c(B)/B; the gap bounds B's smallest prime by about k(p+1) while p = 2(c(B)-1)/(B-c(B)) is about twice that prime, so nothing is bounded absolutely; (ii) exponents are unbounded: c(q^e)/q^e oscillates with e mod 3 between three limits instead of tending to 1, so bounded primes do not bound n. In Lehmer's problem both issues are absent (squarefree, integer target m >= 2). The mod-q valuation that closes omega(B) = 1 gives only congruences for omega(B) = 2 (odd q: exponent != 1 mod 3; (p+2)c(r^b) = 2 mod q). Case B with omega <= 4 is excluded by the ratio bound (product of (1 - 1/q) over 2, 5, 11, 17 is 0.342 > 1/3).
evidence: work/famous/lehmer/README.md (Obstacles); earlier search work/tier2/A123365/probe.py (B = q^a r^b, q, r < 3000, a, b in {2,3,5,6}: no prime p)
next: A Dickson-type argument for fixed prime support (limit equation with each exponent class replaced by its limit ratio; show the limit equation has no exact solution) would bound exponents; the p-versus-B coupling in case A still needs a separate idea.

goal: a cycle of length divisible by 5 under minimum degree >= 5, or any new weaker k = 5 form
obstacle: From a longest path v_0..v_m the visible cycle lengths are p_j - p_i + 2, q_j - q_i + 2, q + m - p + 2, q - p_i + m - p_j + 3. All chord positions from v_0 congruent to 1 and from v_m to m - 1 (mod 3), with m = 1 (mod 3), make every such length 2 (mod 3) at any minimum degree, so path bookkeeping cannot force 0 (mod k). The longest-path layer gives only cycles of length 2 (mod k) for minimum degree >= k + 1.

goal: Lean proof of Dean's conjecture for k = 3 in the formal-conjectures shape
obstacle: The proof (14 pp, JCTB 1994; 10 pp in Choi-Chu-Kim-Park 2026) is a minimal-counterexample analysis over blocks, ears and path lengths mod 3. Mathlib has walks, paths, cycles, take/drop, but no block/cut-vertex or ear decomposition. Done: longest-path lemma, cycle from two chords, cycle of length 2 mod k (min degree k + 1), cycle of length >= k + 1, all in dean_mathlib.lean.
next: Block decomposition and end-block lemma in Lean as the next layer; then the Chen-Saito case analysis.

method_name: Exact constraint search with symmetry breaking (nof2.c)
goal: Finite-field Sylvester-Gallai for transversals: every non-affine permutation of F_p has a 2-point line
obstacle: No counterexample for p <= 19 (p = 19 in 2.5 min). p = 23 is estimated at 30-60 CPU-h (node growth about 30x per prime). Proof attempts through Redei-Megyesi directions, fibre-count degree bounds and the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz do not force <= (p+1)/2 directions.
next: A structural idea that bounds the directions determined by a set with no 2-secant; p = 23 search only if a cheap window appears (it cannot prove the statement).

method_name: Level-to-level matchings (Hopcroft-Karp) joined into a chain partition
goal: Refinement order on integer partitions of n is Sperner
obstacle: Sperner verified for all n <= 90 (56.6M partitions at n = 90; matchings rechecked independently only for n <= 30). Proved only the many-parts end (k >= n/2, merge two 1s). Any chain-partition proof also proves unimodality of p(n,k) in k, known only analytically for large n (Szekeres 1953), with no combinatorial proof.
next: A combinatorial proof of unimodality of p(n,k) would be needed first; otherwise stop.

method_name: Proper floorplan enumeration plus exact elimination (PARI)
goal: Rational equal-area, distinct-perimeter rectangle tiling
obstacle: No rational tiling with n <= 13 tiles (exhaustive over proper floorplans, exact PARI, strict gp mode). n = 14 complete except 80 three-parameter floorplans where the resultant method failed. Rational equal-area tilings exist but always with congruent tiles.
next: Width = 1/height substitution for the 80 open n = 14 floorplans; n = 15 is about 13 CPU-h.

method_name: Bang inequalities plus region weighting, as an LP with cutting planes
goal: Strips covering the unit square minus a square hole of side <= 1/2 have total width >= 1
obstacle: No counterexample (exact IPs: 12 directions, 20x20 grid, delta 0.30-0.50; minimum 1 proved on the grid for delta 0.30, 0.35 and 21/36 positions at 0.40). The Bang-plus-weighting family (which contains the Ambrus et al. 2026 argument) stops at delta ~0.3035 for a corner hole and gives only ~0.82 at delta = 1/2. Nothing certified over continuous angles and offsets.
next: A certified version for delta <= 0.30 needs a Lipschitz bound in the strip angle; reaching 1/2 needs a different idea.

method_name: Explicit prime-gap bound (Schoenfeld) plus exhaustive scan
goal: a(n) = 0 only for the 12 listed n
obstacle: 'If' half reproved (Schoenfeld 1976 Thm 12 plus sieve to 2010760). 'Only if' verified for n <= 1e9. Excluding a bad n for all n needs an upper bound of zero for a prime(-power) pattern in every (rn, rn+r), which sieves cannot give.

obstacle: Bean's 2026 critical sets settle n <= 33 except 27, 28, 30. Products of critical sets are uniquely completable but not minimal for odd bases; necessity checks at n >= 26 exceed 3e5 nodes.

method_name: Reduce to one reverse-and-add orbit plus finite check
goal: The least n with a(n) = 0 are the six listed
obstacle: All six n reach 8877 in one step; every other n <= 3983 reaches a palindrome (checked). Remaining claim: the orbit of 8877 never hits a palindrome, a base-10 Lychrel statement like 196 (no palindrome in 1e6 steps). No proof technique known.

method_name: Block reduction, DFT/permutation conjugacy, minimal-polynomial orders
goal: Closed formula for the order of psi over F_p
obstacle: psi on the f(0)=0 hyperplane is conjugate to DFT(Z/(p-1)) times the discrete-exponential permutation; orders computed for p <= 59 (Lean certifies p = 3, 5, 7, 11), but the factorisation of the characteristic polynomial shows no regularity.
next: Model the factor-degree statistics against random matrices, or find a symmetry of the discrete-exponential permutation that forces factors.

goal: Quantitative Helly for diameter with factor of order d^{-1/2} using 2d sets
obstacle: Best known: 2d sets give diameter <= 2d^2 diam K (Almendra-Hernandez-Ambrus-Kendall 2023); Ivanov-Naszodi show sqrt(d) is optimal but prove only (2d)^3. Ball-containment selection of contact points loses a factor d on the simplex (best hull inradius 1/d), so the proof must use diam K in the selection.
next: Centrally symmetric case with exactly 2d sets via restricted invertibility.
